slides.title: DDD & Microservices Fundamentals
slides.prompt: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) aligns software structures with complex domain models. Core building blocks include Entities (identifiable objects), Value Objects (immutable descriptors), Aggregates (clusters of objects enforcing consistency), and Bounded Contexts (explicit domain boundaries).

slides.title: Value Object Immutability Decorator
slides.prompt: Fill in the `dataclass` option used to enforce immutability for Value Objects.
options: frozen
immutable
static
read_only

slides.title: Entity vs Value Object Key Difference
slides.prompt: What is the defining distinction between an Entity and a Value Object in DDD?
options: An Entity has an explicit identity that persists across state changes, while a Value Object is defined solely by its attributes
An Entity is immutable, while a Value Object can be mutated freely
An Entity cannot be stored in a database, while a Value Object can
An Entity contains only primitive strings, while a Value Object contains complex methods
slides.correctAnswer: An Entity has an explicit identity that persists across state changes, while a Value Object is defined solely by its attributes

slides.title: Aggregate Root Access Control
slides.prompt: Fill in the term for the root entity that controls external access and enforces consistency rules for an Aggregate cluster.
options: Root
Factory
Proxy
Context

slides.title: Bounded Context Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the purpose of defining a 'Bounded Context' in DDD microservice architectures?
options: To set explicit boundaries within which a domain model and its Ubiquitous Language apply strictly
To enforce memory usage limits on microservice Docker containers
To restrict API endpoints to specific IP ranges
To define thread pool limits for async background workers
slides.correctAnswer: To set explicit boundaries within which a domain model and its Ubiquitous Language apply strictly

slides.title: Domain Event Representation
slides.prompt: Fill in the object concept used to notify other parts of a system when something significant happens in the domain.
options: Event
Command
Query
State

slides.title: CQRS Pattern Separation
slides.prompt: What does the CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) architectural pattern separate?
options: It separates read operations (Queries) from write operations (Commands)
It separates Python frontend code from C-extension backend code
It separates thread locks from process signals
It separates database connection pooling from garbage collection
slides.correctAnswer: It separates read operations (Queries) from write operations (Commands)
